Representative_Docs: ['I was nervous a little before the speech task, I’ve never really done vr before so it was a very new experience for me. Once the evaluators appeared, it kind of threw me for a loop because I wasn’t sure what to expect. In general when I speak to others I don’t make a ton of eye contact, and especially once I realized the evaluators were changing reactions seemingly at random I did not pay much attention to how they reacted. I gave pretty genuine answers in the speech, I did not feel it was super polished, but I didn’t feel like it needed to be because of who was hearing it. The random reactions were pretty funny to me so I had to really work to focus on the task, and the stakes felt super low because the people weren’t real.', 'I was surprised when the two judges on the ends of the table seemed to change reactions. When the judge on the left first started to show signs of disinterest and negative reactions, I had a hard time concentrating on what I was saying, and then I felt nervous because I realized that some of the things I was saying didn’t really make much sense. When I looked at the judge on the right, I was surprised to see that he looked encouraging and supportive, since my first impression of him was that he would be a tough critic. When the judge on the left started to look more positive and smiling, I felt proud. But when the judge on the right started to look critical and more negative, I felt anxious that I had made a bad impression. I couldn’t tell if the judge in the middle was even paying much attention since he was so neutral, but I didn’t feel much anxiety when looking at him.', 'It was hard to stay focused when the evaluator’s reactions kept changing. After getting thrown off by an evaluator losing interest, I stopped focusing on the evaluators and focused as much as I could on making my statements calm and connected to each other. I kept talking and tried to avoid pauses as much as I could. Afterwards, it was hard not to be annoyed with myself for not giving a word-perfect summary of my resume and getting distracted/stumbling over words. It was especially tough since I tend to do very well in job interviews! I had to remind myself that this was an extra hard task different from a real job interview where I could count on reliable reactions from interviewers + a job description that I didn’t make up on the spot 3 minutes ago. It was also tough that all the evaluators were white men, making me feel less comfortable than female evaluators.']
